back_translation: "But now listen, O Jacob My servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
Thus says the LORD who made you, who formed you from the womb, who will help you: Do not fear, O Jacob My servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the parched ground. I will pour My Spirit on your offspring and My blessing on your descendants.
They will sprout up among the grass, like willows by flowing streams.
One will say, 'I belong to the LORD'; another will call himself by the name of Jacob; another will write on his hand, 'Belonging to the LORD,' and take the name Israel as his surname."
Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel and his Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts: "I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God at all.
Who is like Me? Let him proclaim it! Let him declare and lay it out before Me, since I established the ancient people. Let them declare the things to come and what will happen.
Do not tremble and do not be afraid. Have I not told you and declared it long ago? You are My witnesses! Is there any God besides Me? There is none. There is no other Rock; I know not a single one."
All who form idols are emptiness, and the things they delight in are worthless. Their own witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so they will be put to shame.
Who would form a god or cast an idol that profits him nothing at all?
Behold, all his companions will be put to shame, and the craftsmen are merely human. Let them all assemble and take their stand; they will be terrified and put to shame together.

The blacksmith takes a tool and works over the coals; he shapes an idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arm. Indeed, he gets hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.

The carpenter stretches out a measuring line; he sketches the outline with a stylus, carves it with chisels, and marks its circle with a compass. He makes it in the shape of a man, with human beauty, to set up in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars for himself, or chooses a cypress or an oak and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.

Then it becomes fuel for a man. He takes some of it to warm himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread. Then he makes a god of part of it and bows down to it; he makes a carved idol and prostrates himself before it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over that half he roasts meat. He eats his fill and even warms himself, saying, "Ah! How warm and cozy — I see the fire!"
From the rest he makes a god, his carved idol. He prostrates himself before it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Save me, for you are my god."
They do not know and do not understand, for their eyes are plastered shut so they cannot see, and their hearts are closed so they cannot understand.

No one reflects in his heart; there is no knowledge or understanding to say, "I burned half of it in the fire; I even baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and ate. Shall I then make something detestable from the rest? Shall I prostrate myself before a block of wood?"
He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has led him astray. He cannot save his own life, nor can he say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
"Remember these things, O Jacob, O Israel, for you are My servant. I formed you; you are My servant, O Israel; you will not be forgotten by Me.
I have blotted out your transgressions like a thick cloud, and your sins like the morning mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you."

Sing for joy, O heavens, for the LORD has done this! Shout aloud, O depths of the earth! Break forth into song, O mountains, O forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and He will display His glory in Israel.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: "I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by Myself,
who frustrates the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who overturns the wise and turns their knowledge into folly,

who confirms the word of His servant and fulfills the counsel of His messengers, who says of Jerusalem, 'She will be inhabited,' and of the cities of Judah, 'They will be rebuilt, and I will raise up their ruins,'
who says to the depths of the sea, 'Be dry!' and 'I will dry up your currents,'
who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd, and he will accomplish all that I please,' who says of Jerusalem, 'She will be rebuilt,' and of the temple, 'Your foundation will be laid.'"
